text:
Nina Park: quick sync - been seeing irregular p95 increases traced to the continuous-batcher. looks like eviction and requeue cycles are the common pattern. want to discuss long-term changes vs short-term mitigations.
Owen Blake: agree. short term we can reduce aggressive eviction and add a soft-evict that prefers oldest partial windows rather than wholesale flush. long term we should rethink admission + fairness.
Ravi Shah: long-term idea: split the work into two paths: small-window fast-path (strict latency) and pack-path (packing-first). route by declared intent or inferred request size. helps avoid one-size-fits-all pressure.
Nina Park: path split is attractive but impacts backpressure surface and tracing. need clear interface: admission API should return (route=fast|pack, expected_tokens) and a decision span.
Owen Blake: tradeoffs: split increases code paths and testing burden. also can double memory for metadata if we maintain per-path queues. but it isolates heavy packing logic from latency-sensitive flows.
Ravi Shah: alternative: keep unified queue but add admission hints and a small priority score. admission_score = weight(tenant_tier) + hint_latency_penalty + dynamic_starvation_adjustment. scheduler uses score to place in micro-lanes. cheaper than two full code paths.
Nina Park: micro-lanes idea reduces memory overhead but needs careful fairness — we must prevent low-score requests from starving. propose min-share guarantees per tenant_bucket.
Owen Blake: accepted. also propose lease-like admission: when a request enters a micro-lane, it holds a soft-lease for N tokens worth of capacity to avoid immediate eviction mid-generation. helps reduce wasted work.
Ravi Shah: soft-lease avoids thrash but increases headroom reservation. use small N (e.g., 8-16 tokens) and make it configurable per lane.
Nina Park: instrumentation plan: emit lane_assignment, admission_score, lease_acquired(true|false), evict_reason (overflow|policy|ttl), and pack_loss_tokens histogram. correlate by worker_id and tenant_bucket.
Owen Blake: can we add a lightweight supervisor that watches oscillation frequency per-worker and temporarily forces conservative mode (disable extension) if oscillation > threshold? local auto-protect.
Ravi Shah: yes. supervisor state can be tiny: last_flip_ts and flip_count windowed. if flip_count high, engage cool-down for 1s.
Nina Park: rollout strategy for experiments: implement micro-lanes + lease in feature-flagged build, test in staging, then 5% canary for 2h with metrics: pack_efficiency_delta, p99/p95 latency delta, pack_loss_tokens, and queue_oscillation_rate. abort if p99 > baseline + 25ms or pack_efficiency drops >5%.
Owen Blake: dev tasks: 1) add admission_score calc and lane assignment (Owen), 2) implement soft-lease + eviction policy (Ravi), 3) metrics + tracing spans (Nina).
infra-bot: canary build queued by Nina P. feature flag: continuous_batcher.micro_lanes=true. :rocket:
Ravi Shah: will add minimal unit tests for lease semantics and a stress test to reproduce oscillation locally.
Nina Park: thanks. keep follow-ups minimal here; we'll post a short summary after the canary.
